newsitem.title: USA: Weekly jobless claims rose in latest week.
newsitem.headline: Weekly jobless claims rose in latest week.

text.p: The number of people lining up for first-time unemployment benefits rose last week, the government said on Thursday.
The Labour Department said 332,000 Americans filed initial claims for jobless benefits in the week ended April 12, up from a revised 324,000 in the previous week.
Wall Street economists on average had expected claims of 317,000 in the week ended April 12.

The four-week moving average of claims -- viewed as a more reliable gauge of jobless trends because it smooths out weekly fluctuations -- rose to 319,750 last week from a revised 315,250 in the prior week.

Total benefit rolls climbed to 2.32 million in the week ended April 5, the latest period for which that data were available, the department said. Ongoing jobless claims stood at 2.3 million in the previous week.
The department said 15 states reported increases in claims exceeding 1,000 on an unadjusted basis in the week ended April 5, the latest period for which that data were available.
Among the largest were New Jersey with 4,576, California with 3,606, North Carolina with 3,470, New York with 3,436, and Pennsylvania with 3,322.

New Jersey reported layoffs in the construction, trade and service industries. North Carolina said it had layoffs in the textile industry, while New York attributed the increase to layoffs in the service industry.
Pennsylvania reported layoffs in the food, electrical equipment, and lumber and wood industries. California gave no reason for its increase in claims.
Two states reported a drop in claims of more than 1,000. They were Georgia with 1,247 and Virginia with 1,096.
Georgia reported fewer layoffs in the automobile and transportation equipment industries and Virginia said it had fewer layoffs in the furniture industry.
